Remodeling Old Houses is Heimer Family Tradition 

"I am a second generation contractor and grew up spending time on job sites. I watched neglected buildings get transformed into beautiful homes. I forged by own path in the construction industry starting in 2009. I have worked in different corners of the construction industry from commercial construction, bathroom remodeling,  and new cosntrcution. In 2018 I started Heimer Remodeling Enterprises to blend all of my unique experiences together.  I care about our customers and I value communication. I am personally invested in every project and never turn a job over until it meets my expectations. It is my passion, and in a way, a family tradition to breathe new life into old houses."

At Heimer Remodeling, we offer a comprehensive suite of services tailored to elevate your living spaces to new heights of luxury and functionality. From conceptualization to execution, our dedicated team oversees every aspect of the design process, ensuring seamless integration of your vision into reality. Whether it's a stunning kitchen transformation, a rejuvenating bathroom remodel, or a complete overhaul of your entire home, our expertise in full-house renovation and restoration guarantees exceptional results. We handle every detail, from demolition and clean-out to the installation of custom cabinets, meticulous painting, and flawless tile and flooring execution, leaving no stone unturned in delivering a space that exceeds your expectations.

Refine Remodel is a local remodeling company proudly serving the Evansville, Indiana area. We combine practical expertise with thoughtful design to transform houses into comfortable, functional homes. Our team brings years of experience in remodeling and exterior improvements, backed by a commitment to clear communication and dependable results.

Why we’re different

Client-first approach: We place your needs, preferences, and budget at the center of every project. From the initial consultation to final walkthrough, we prioritize transparency, timely communication, and respect for your home.

Quality workmanship: Skilled craftsmen and reliable subcontractors ensure projects are completed to high standards. We use proven materials and best practices to deliver durable, attractive results that stand up to daily life and the Midwest climate.

Comprehensive services: Rather than focusing on one trade, we handle a broad range of projects so you have a single point of contact and consistent quality across work scopes. This reduces coordination headaches and keeps timelines predictable.

Local focus: Serving Evansville and nearby communities allows us to respond quickly, understand local building conditions and codes, and build long-term relationships with our clients and suppliers.

Accountability and follow-through: We provide detailed project plans, clear pricing, and defined timelines. When issues arise, we address them promptly and professionally.

Siding replacement and repair

Window and door installation

Charleston’s Trusted General Contractor
for High-Quality Residential Construction

When homeowners in Charleston need a general contractor they can trust, they turn to Canter Construction.

We specialize in residential construction, remodeling, and renovation projects built with precision, transparency, and long-term value in mind. From full home renovations and kitchen remodels to additions and complex structural projects, our team brings a process-driven approach to construction that eliminates guesswork and delivers consistent results. 

Homeowners across Charleston, Mount Pleasant, James Island, and West Ashley choose Canter Construction because we prioritize quality craftsmanship, clear communication, and accountability at every stage of the build. Unlike contractors who rely on shortcuts or one-size-fits-all solutions, we approach every project with careful planning, specialized trades, and hands-on project management — ensuring your home is built the right way, not just the fastest way.

What Sets Canter Construction Apart

Choosing a general contractor isn’t just about finding someone who can build; it’s about finding a team that can plan, manage, and execute a complex project without costly surprises. That’s where Canter Construction stands apart.

Our work is built on a process-first construction model. Every project begins with detailed planning, realistic budgeting, and a clear scope of work before construction starts. We don’t rely on vague estimates or last-minute decisions in the field. Instead, we coordinate specialized subcontractors, schedules, materials, and inspections upfront so your project stays organized, efficient, and predictable.

Unlike many contractors who stretch crews thin or rely on general labor for highly technical work, we partner with trade-specific professionals — experienced carpenters, electricians, plumbers, and finish specialists who focus on what they do best. This approach delivers higher-quality results, better timelines, and fewer compromises during construction.

Most importantly, we believe transparency builds trust. Homeowners work directly with a professional team that communicates clearly, documents decisions, and takes responsibility for every phase of the project — from the first walkthrough to final completion.

Work With Us
Our Construction Process

At Canter Construction, we believe great results come from a clear, repeatable process — not guesswork. Our approach is designed to eliminate confusion, reduce delays, and give homeowners confidence at every stage of the project.

Discovery & Planning

We start by understanding your goals, your home, and how you plan to use the space. This includes site evaluations, budget alignment, and early feasibility conversations so expectations are set correctly from day one.

Design Coordination & Scope Definition

Whether we’re working with your designer or coordinating design internally, we define the scope in detail before construction begins. Materials, layouts, finishes, and structural considerations are aligned early to avoid mid-project changes.

Pre-Construction Preparation

Permits, schedules, subcontractor coordination, and material ordering are handled before work starts. This phase is critical for keeping timelines realistic and preventing costly disruptions once construction is underway.

Build Phase & Project Management

Your project is managed by experienced professionals who coordinate trade specialists, inspections, and progress milestones. We prioritize communication, cleanliness, and consistency so your home remains as functional as possible during construction.

Final Walkthrough & Completion

Every project ends with a detailed walkthrough to ensure craftsmanship, finishes, and functionality meet our standards — and yours. Our job isn’t finished until the space is complete and ready to be enjoyed.

This process allows us to deliver high-quality residential construction with fewer surprises, tighter timelines, and results that stand the test of time.

Work With Us
Who We Serve

Canter Construction works with homeowners who value quality, clear communication, and long-term results. Our clients aren’t looking for the cheapest option — they’re looking for the right partner to execute their vision correctly the first time.

We typically work with:

Primary homeowners planning thoughtful remodels that improve daily living

Second-home and coastal property owners who need a reliable local general contractor they can trust

Growing families expanding or reconfiguring their homes for functionality and comfort

Design-forward clients who care deeply about finishes, layouts, and craftsmanship

Real estate–savvy homeowners who understand the value of doing projects the right way for resale and longevity

Our projects range from full home remodels and custom builds to kitchens, bathrooms, exterior construction, and complex renovations that require experienced coordination across multiple trades.

Because we are deeply familiar with Charleston-area construction requirements — including permitting, zoning, historic considerations, and coastal building conditions — we’re able to guide clients through projects that would otherwise feel overwhelming.

If you’re looking for a Charleston general contractor who brings structure, transparency, and pride of workmanship to every project, you’re in the right place.

Work With Us
Charleston & Lowcountry Construction Expertise

Canter Construction is built around a deep understanding of what it takes to construct and remodel homes in the Charleston and Lowcountry region. This isn’t just where we work — it’s where we’ve spent years navigating the realities of coastal construction.

Building in Charleston is different than building almost anywhere else. Between humidity, salt air, flood zones, historic overlays, and evolving building codes, experience matters.

Our team is fluent in:

Charleston-area permitting and inspections

Historic district and design review considerations

Coastal construction best practices for durability and longevity

Flood zone requirements and elevation planning

This guide is designed for homeowners looking to remodel their bathrooms for improved functionality and aesthetics. The inspiration for this project type can lead to a modern and efficient space that enhances daily routines.

What Homeowners Should Know Before Starting

Budgeting for a bathroom remodel requires careful planning, as costs can vary widely based on materials and labor. Timing is crucial; expect the project to take several weeks, depending on the scope of work. Hiring licensed tradespeople, such as plumbers and electricians, is essential for complex installations. Before work begins, clear the area and consider temporary bathroom solutions. Common mistakes include underestimating the importance of ventilation and neglecting to plan for storage solutions.

How This Work Is Typically Built

For a bathroom remodel, focus on plumbing and electrical layouts, ensuring they comply with local codes. Framing may need adjustments for new fixtures, while drywall installation should consider moisture-resistant materials. Tile installation requires proper substrate preparation, and waterproofing is critical in wet areas. Ensure that all fixtures, such as sinks and toilets, are securely anchored and that the shower area has adequate drainage.

Materials & Finish Options Compared

When selecting materials, consider options like ceramic tiles versus natural stone for flooring and walls. Ceramic tiles are generally more affordable and easier to maintain, while natural stone offers a luxurious look but requires more upkeep. For countertops, quartz is durable and non-porous, while granite provides a unique aesthetic but may need sealing. Choose materials that can withstand the humidity of a bathroom environment.

Planning & Layout Considerations

Layout is vital; ensure that the flow between the sink, toilet, and shower is logical and functional. Consider natural light sources and artificial lighting placement to enhance visibility. Access to plumbing and electrical systems should be planned for future maintenance. Sequence the work carefully, starting with demolition, followed by plumbing and electrical updates, and finishing with fixtures and finishes.

Maintenance & Long-Term Care

Regular maintenance of bathroom fixtures includes checking for leaks and ensuring proper sealing around tiles and countertops. Clean surfaces with appropriate cleaners to prevent mold and mildew buildup. Periodically inspect caulking and grout lines, replacing them as necessary to maintain water resistance.

Safety, Codes & Permits

Bathroom remodels may require permits for plumbing and electrical work, which should be verified with your local building department. Safety practices include ensuring proper ventilation to prevent moisture buildup and using GFCI outlets in wet areas. Always consult with a licensed contractor to navigate local codes and regulations.

Professional Recommendations

Hiring a licensed contractor is advisable for complex bathroom remodels, especially when plumbing and electrical work is involved. Quality checkpoints include verifying that all materials meet local code requirements and that installations are performed correctly. Regular communication with your contractor can help ensure the project stays on track and within budget.

This guide is for homeowners looking to enhance their property's curb appeal with a wooden fence. A well-constructed fence not only provides privacy but also adds aesthetic value to your home. The image serves as inspiration for creating a charming outdoor space with floral accents and a classic fence design.

What Homeowners Should Know Before Starting

When planning a wooden fence installation, consider your budget and timeline, as costs can vary based on materials and labor. It's essential to hire experienced tradespeople to ensure quality workmanship and compliance with local regulations. Before starting, check property lines and obtain any necessary permits to avoid disputes. Common mistakes include neglecting to treat wood for weather resistance and failing to plan for maintenance access.

How This Work Is Typically Built

For a wooden fence, begin by selecting the right type of wood, such as cedar or redwood, known for their durability and resistance to decay. Ensure proper post spacing, typically 6-8 feet apart, and use concrete footings to anchor the posts securely. Consider the design of the fence, whether it's a picket style or solid panel, and ensure that the panels are properly attached to the posts. Don't forget to include a gate for access, reinforcing the gate posts for stability.

Materials & Finish Options Compared

Common materials for wooden fences include cedar, redwood, and pressure-treated pine. Cedar is naturally resistant to rot and insects, making it a popular choice, while redwood offers a rich color and longevity but can be more expensive. Pressure-treated pine is budget-friendly but requires regular maintenance to prevent decay. Each material has its pros and cons regarding cost, durability, and maintenance needs, so choose based on your specific requirements.

Planning & Layout Considerations

When planning your wooden fence, consider the layout and how it will complement your landscaping. Ensure that the design allows for adequate sunlight and access to your garden areas. Think about the height of the fence for privacy and security, and consult local regulations regarding maximum allowable heights. Additionally, plan the sequence of installation to minimize disruption to your yard and surrounding areas.

Maintenance & Long-Term Care

Regular maintenance is crucial for the longevity of your wooden fence. This includes periodic cleaning, staining, or sealing to protect against moisture and UV damage. Inspect the fence annually for signs of rot or insect damage and replace any compromised boards promptly. Keeping vegetation trimmed away from the fence will also help prevent moisture buildup and promote airflow.

Safety, Codes & Permits

Installing a wooden fence may require permits, depending on local regulations, particularly concerning height and placement near property lines. It's advisable to verify with your local building department to ensure compliance with any zoning laws. Safety practices during installation include wearing protective gear and ensuring that all tools are used according to manufacturer guidelines.

Professional Recommendations

Hiring a licensed contractor can ensure that your wooden fence is built to last and complies with local codes. Look for professionals who have experience with fence installation and can provide references. Quality checkpoints include verifying the quality of materials used, ensuring proper post installation, and confirming that the design meets your aesthetic and functional needs.

This guide is for homeowners looking to upgrade their driveway with decorative concrete. The image showcases a beautifully designed concrete driveway that enhances the overall aesthetic of a home.

Homeowner Notes

Budgeting for a decorative concrete driveway involves considering material costs, labor, and potential site preparation. Timing is crucial; plan for weather conditions, as concrete should not be poured in extreme temperatures. Hiring experienced tradespeople is essential for quality results; ensure they have a solid portfolio. Before work begins, clear the area of debris and ensure proper drainage to avoid future issues. Common mistakes include underestimating the importance of a solid base and neglecting to account for expansion joints.

Construction Details

For a decorative concrete driveway, start with proper site preparation, which includes grading and compacting the sub-base. Ensure adequate drainage to prevent water pooling. Use forms to shape the driveway and pour concrete, ensuring it is leveled and finished properly. Consider adding decorative elements like stamping or staining before the concrete sets. Finally, ensure that expansion joints are placed to accommodate movement and prevent cracking.

Materials Detail

Concrete driveways can be made from standard concrete, stamped concrete, or colored concrete. Standard concrete is durable and cost-effective but lacks visual appeal. Stamped concrete offers a variety of designs and textures, enhancing aesthetics but may require more maintenance. Colored concrete can add vibrancy but may fade over time. Each option has its pros and cons, so consider your budget and desired look when choosing materials.

Planning Considerations

When planning your driveway, consider the layout for optimal access and functionality. Ensure the design complements your home’s architecture and landscaping. Proper lighting is essential for safety and aesthetics; consider incorporating lighting features along the driveway. Access for vehicles and pedestrians should be seamless, and plan for any necessary grading to ensure a smooth transition from the street to your driveway.

Maintenance Care

Regular maintenance for a decorative concrete driveway includes sealing every few years to protect against stains and weather damage. Clean the surface periodically to prevent dirt buildup and use a pressure washer for tougher stains. Repair any cracks promptly to prevent further damage, and ensure that drainage systems remain clear to avoid water pooling.

Safety, Code, and Permits

Installing a concrete driveway may require permits, depending on local regulations. Check with your local building department to ensure compliance with zoning laws and safety codes. Safety practices include using proper personal protective equipment during installation and ensuring that the area is secure to prevent accidents during construction.

Professional Recommendations

Hiring a licensed contractor is advisable for a decorative concrete driveway to ensure quality and adherence to local codes. Look for contractors with experience in decorative concrete work and check their references. Quality checkpoints include verifying the materials used, ensuring proper site preparation, and confirming that the final finish meets your design expectations.

Conclusion

A well-planned approach helps you avoid costly surprises and get results that match how you actually use your home.

We serve San Diego County and surrounding communities, including La Jolla, Del Mar, Carlsbad, Encinitas, Oceanside, Escondido, Chula Vista, Poway, San Marcos, Solana Beach, Pacific Beach, Point Loma, Coronado, and El Cajon.

What remodeling services do you offer?

We offer complete home remodeling, kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, home additions and room additions, accessory dwelling unit (ADU) construction, custom home builds, new construction, outdoor living spaces, roof replacement, blueprints and engineering, energy-efficient solutions, and exclusive 3D rendering.

How much does a home remodel cost in San Diego?

Project cost depends on scope, size, materials, and finishes. We provide a detailed, itemized estimate after a free consultation so you know the cost before work begins.

Do you provide free consultations and estimates?

Yes. We offer free consultations and detailed written estimates. Call (877) 263-4346 or request a quote through our contact page to schedule a meeting with our design team.

How long does a typical remodeling project take?

Timelines vary by scope. Bathroom remodels often take 3–6 weeks, kitchen remodels 6–12 weeks, and whole-home renovations or ADUs several months. We provide a project schedule up front and keep you updated throughout construction.

THE SERVICES WE OFFER

PRESSURE WASHING SERVICE

Our pressure washing service will keep your home's exterior looking fresh and clean. Remove dirt, mold, and grime that build up over time with our powerful washing solutions. Pressure washing is perfect for maintaining your driveways and other surfaces to ensure long-lasting curb appeal.

Protect your home from further harm with our professional water damage mitigation services. Our team acts quickly to extract moisture, dry affected areas, and prevent mold growth after leaks or flooding. INTERIOR PAINTING SERVICES

Revitalize the interior of your home with our professional interior painting services. You can choose from a variety of color options that will transform any room into a beautiful, personalized space. KITCHEN REMODELING

Trust us to modernize your living spaces with high-quality materials and professional design.

BASEMENT RENOVATION

Maximize your home's usable space with our expert basement renovation services. We transform unfinished or outdated basements into functional living areas, such as home theaters, guest suites, or home offices. Our team focuses on moisture control, insulation, and high-end finishes to ensure your new space is both comfortable and durable.

We utilize premium paints and expert techniques to deliver a vibrant, lasting finish that protects your surfaces and enhances aesthetics. From color consultation to the final touch-ups, we ensure a seamless and stress-free experience.

Some of the home remodeling services we specialize in are:
Whole House Renovation

The best way to fall in love with your house again is by completely renovating it so that you can create your dream home. Upgrade all of your appliances, windows, doors, kitchen, baths, and floors. Greaves Construction is a Tampa -Temple Terrace home remodeling company that can give you a whole new design to your tired house. If you are going to renovate, you might as well go all the way.

Kitchen and Bathroom Remodeling

Kitchens and bathrooms are the most common areas to renovate. These are the two areas that you spend most of your time in. If you are still working with grill top stoves it is time to convert to electric stove tops. If you are showering in a tiny tub with a standard shower head it is time to expand that tub and maybe even upgrade to a sauna/steam unit.

1&2 Story Additions

Instead of expanding within your home, have you ever considered expanding on top of your house? If you already live in a one story house and are interested in adding a second story to create more rooms, this is most efficient way. Maybe you need extra rooms for your growing family. Or maybe you are interested in creating a whole floor as your master bedroom. There is no problem with wanting more space for yourself. Our home remodeling company in Tampa/Temple Terrace is equipped to give you the additional space as needed.

Historic Renovation and Restoration

Historic houses have an elegant quality to them that can get lost over the years. What was attractive when the house was first purchased can now be falling apart due to how old the house is. To regain the aesthetic of an historical house, our Tampa/Temple Terrace home remodeling company can reproduce any aspect of the house that is tarnished. For instance, if white columns are what makes the house historically appealing, Greaves Construction can rebuild them so that the chips and cracks in the paint are gone. This will allow the house to remain historic without looking neglected.

Universal Design

Modern homes are all the rage nowadays. People are falling in love the accessibility of walk-in tubs and elevator lifts within their homes. Convenience is the latest trend when it comes to homes. If you are the type of person that enjoys spending time in your kitchen, but hates how small it is, we can take down the barriers and expand your kitchen giving you more room to work with.

FBC REMODELING’S
Home Remodeling Process

Do you want a beautiful kitchen? How about a basement that flows with the rest of your home? If you are looking for a truly remarkable space, then follow these simple steps as we walk you through our design-build process. Our process puts the homeowner first, and we make sure our clients are comfortable with our team, process, and design before they even spend a dime.

STEP 1
Build Joy Call

The first step of our process is an introductory call with you and our design coordinator.

STEP 2
Virtual Consultation

We’ll discuss your existing space, your vision, your lifestyle, and your hopes for your remodel to establish how your project will move forward.

STEP 3
Measure

A designer will come to your home to measure your existing space and take photos to begin developing your design plans.

STEP 4
Ideas Meeting

This is a collaborative meeting where you can work with your designer to identify design features you want in your finished space.

STEP 5
Production Walk

This is the perfect time to ask any questions you have regarding the build process.

STEP 6
Plan Review

We will talk to you about your project, scope of work, and budget to determine if we may be a good fit for you and help answer your initial questions!

STEP 7
Selections Meeting

It’s time to select materials for your space! You and your designer will head to a design center where you will find the perfect styles and colors to complete your space and make it your own.

STEP 8
Pre-Construction Meeting

Your project manager and superintendent will come to your home to walk through the space again in preparation for construction.

STEP 9
Construction Begins

Construction begins! We’ll handle permitting, order all materials, and provide a detailed schedule.

STEP 10
Mid-Project Review

At the mid-project inspection point, your entire project team will come out to walk the space and ensure your project is on track.

STEP 11
Final Project Review

You'll receive a final inspection from your permitting authority, a walk-through with your project team, and another opportunity to complete a survey review of your experience.

STEP 12
Warranty

Every FBC Remodel project is under warranty. You can always contact us to resolve any issues with your project.

WHY WE DO WHAT WE DO
About FBC Remodel

At FBC Remodel, our purpose is our why. We are driven by building joy, and we do what we do – and do it well – to build joy for as many people as possible.

To us, building joy does not simply mean for our clients. We build joy from the inside out, starting with our team first. Having a happy team has an incredible effect on a business. Joy and happiness cascade down the pipeline from the internal team, through our trades, and down to our clients. We aim to build joy at each step and with each process, both inside and out.

We take care of ourselves through Build Joy principles and take those principles into everything we do. Build Joy has the incredible effect of creating an atmosphere that fosters success and well-being within the company, allowing our team to perform far and above expectations.

As a company, our core values are Team First, Unstoppable, Own Our Results, We Are What We Speak, and Coachable. Each of these values plays a significant role in how FBC Remodel operates for our own employees and our clients. When you have a team like ours that is on the same page, working by the same values, and passionately loves what they do, the outcome is magical.

WE CARE.
What Makes FBC Remodel Different

Our team obsessively cares about your experience, your outcome, and you! We are passionately driven to create stunning spaces that bring joy to your home. As such, we have proven processes in place that ensure a no-stress, exciting experience from start to finish. With over 20 years in the remodeling industry, we have had plenty of time to edit and refine these processes, and while we know they work, we are constantly looking for ways to be better and grow.

FBC has mastered the art of listening. We take time to learn about you and what home means for your life. Our collaborative process has evolved into the best home renovation practices in the industry and results in a superior space that fits — and improves — your life by designing your home around you.

FBC Remodel was designed to be different. We are committed to building joy through remodeling with passionate, award-winning interior designers, skilled craftsmen, inspiring showrooms, and a transparent construction process.

Experience The FBC Difference
No Headaches Construction

You’ll not only experience great design, but you’ll truly appreciate our finely-tuned construction management process.

Our project managers are highly organized and attentive to detail, not to mention excellent choreographers of the many phases of construction.

High Quality Craftsmanship

Projects with FBC are well-managed, and construction is of the highest quality. We maintain relationships with all local building jurisdictions to ensure that your project is completed to code and passes all inspections. When it comes to finishing touches, you have infinite choices— from simplicity to pure luxury.

Quick & Efficient Completion

You might be surprised at how quickly you’ll enjoy your new space. We take pride in fast, but efficient, projects.

FBC’s scheduling and build process are the tightest in the industry, which means many projects are typically complete in just 10 – 12 weeks.

It All Started With A Basement Remodel

In the fall of 1997, the editor of the Rocky Mountain News’ Spotlight Section was browsing the Fall Home Show and was intrigued by a new company offering a service she had never seen before: specialty basement finishing. She did her research and interviews and wrote an article. Two weeks later (and three days before our phones were connected), the Rocky Mountain News published a front-page article featuring our exciting new organization: Finished Basement Company.

At Finished Basement Company, we designed and built basements — great basements. Since our formation, we’ve finished more basements than anyone in the nation while developing into a premier design-build firm specializing solely in basement remodels.

A funny thing happened, though. All those basements we finished had happy families enjoying them, and they wanted the rest of their homes to feel as well-designed as their basements. How could we say no? Now, twenty-plus years later, our design/build process is available for any part of your home — kitchens, living rooms, bathrooms, bedrooms, and specialty spaces — because we’re determined to create great spaces that matter.

FBC Remodel - Your Design Firm

We design and build beautiful, custom spaces that will bring you joy for years to come. Through our proven design-build process, we are dedicated to creating the space of your dreams and doing it in a timely, effective, and open manner. We promise to listen to you every step of the way and make sure that the process and your final product is above and beyond your expectations.

Our 20+ years in the remodeling business have given us an edge that works in your favor. From basements to kitchens, bathrooms, and offices, we are more than equipped to meet precisely where you are and bring you where you want to be. Our expert team will diligently work to bring your dream to life and create a space that is uniquely and incredibly you.

FOUNDER
DAVID PERROTTI

Connecticut Design-Build Remodeling Expert | Veteran | Author

David Perrotti is the founder of Fine Home Contracting, a Connecticut-based design-build remodeling company specializing in luxury home additions, whole-house renovations, high-end kitchens, and large-scale residential remodeling projects.

Since founding Fine Home Contracting in 2012, David has helped homeowners transform their homes through a planning-first design-build process that emphasizes communication, organization, craftsmanship, and attention to detail.

With more than 20 years of construction experience, over 350 completed remodeling projects, and more than $17 million in completed residential construction, David has built a reputation for delivering highly detailed projects while creating a remodeling experience that homeowners can actually enjoy.

Today, Fine Home Contracting focuses on complex remodeling projects typically ranging from $600,000 to $2 million throughout Connecticut.

ABOUT ME
MY STORY

My journey into construction began at Oliver Wolcott Technical High School in Torrington, Connecticut, where I studied carpentry and developed a passion for building.

After graduation, I worked for a general contractor and learned the fundamentals of residential construction before joining the United States Army in 2001 as a Military Police soldier.

I deployed to Iraq from 2003–2004 and later joined the United States Air Force, deploying again to Iraq from 2007–2008.

The military taught me lessons that continue to influence every aspect of how we run Fine Home Contracting today:

Planning matters.
Communication matters.
Accountability matters.
Attention to detail matters.
Teams perform best when expectations are clear.

Between deployments and after returning home, I worked as a finish carpenter while earning a degree in Business Management. In 2012, I founded Fine Home Contracting with a simple goal:

To raise the standard of remodeling by combining exceptional craftsmanship with exceptional client experience.

Over the years, I noticed many contractors focused primarily on construction while overlooking the homeowner experience. Projects suffered from poor communication, unrealistic expectations, inadequate planning, and lack of organization.

I believed homeowners deserved better.

That belief became the foundation of Fine Home Contracting.

MORE THAN A HOME
MY PHILOSOPHY ON HOME DESIGN

I believe your home should be more than a place where you live. It should be your sanctuary.

A home should create peace. It should be a place where memories are made, where families gather, where you can recharge from the demands of everyday life, and where the environment around you supports the life you want to live.

The spaces we live in affect us more than most people realize. The layout of a room, the flow between spaces, the natural light, the materials we touch every day, and the overall design all influence how we feel and interact with our environment.

A primary bathroom is not simply a bathroom. It is where you begin your day and where you end it. Along with the bedroom, it should evoke peace, comfort, order, and well-being.

A kitchen is not simply a place to prepare meals. It is often the heart of the home. It should encourage family connection, make cooking enjoyable, and create opportunities for people to spend time together.

The best homes have a feeling when you walk through the door.

They feel intentional.
They feel comfortable.
They reflect the people who live there.

That is why I believe the design phase is the most important part of any remodeling project. Before construction begins, we focus on understanding how you live, what matters most to your family, and how your home can better support your lifestyle.

At Fine Home Contracting, we believe you cannot over-plan and you cannot over-communicate. Great remodeling projects happen when thoughtful design, detailed planning, and expert craftsmanship come together to create a home that feels uniquely yours. My goal is not simply to build beautiful spaces. My goal is to help homeowners create homes they genuinely love being in every day.

WHAT I LEARNED
LESSONS FROM 350+ REMODELING PROJECTS

After completing hundreds of remodeling projects throughout Connecticut, a few principles consistently prove true:

1. You Cannot Over-Plan: The best projects are won before construction starts. Detailed planning reduces surprises, delays, and unnecessary costs.

2. Communication Solves Problems Early: Most construction problems begin as communication problems. Clear expectations create better outcomes for everyone involved.

3. The Design Phase Determines Success: The more decisions made before construction begins, the smoother the project will run.

4. Materials Matter: The materials you choose influence not only durability and maintenance but also how your home feels every day.

5. Remodeling Is About Improving Life: Beautiful spaces are important, but the real goal is creating a home that functions better for the people who live there.

6. Quality Is Never an Accident: Quality comes from planning, skilled craftsmanship, attention to detail, and consistent execution.

7. Experience Matters: Every remodeling project presents unique challenges. Experience allows problems to be solved before they become expensive mistakes.

5 STEPS TO YOUR NEW SPACE
Our Design Process

When you choose Renovation By Design, you’re partnering with a team of passionate designers and skilled remodelers who put your vision at the heart of everything we do.

Our mission is to deliver a finished space that not only meets your goals—but exceeds your expectations. From start to finish, we’re committed to providing a renovation experience that’s seamless, collaborative, and stress free. Call RBD today at (248) 260-7639.

SCHEDULE A CONSULTATION
STEP ONE
Discovery

During this phase in our process, we will invite you into our showroom for a complimentary consultation where we will review your project scope and investment expectations. During your showroom tour, you will be able to view different cabinet lines, countertops, and many more selection ideas.

STEP TWO
Design Planning

Once we’ve received a Design Retainer, we will conduct a site visit to document your existing conditions, measure, and photograph the areas that will be affected by your project. We will then create a concept design and a preliminary investment range for your project outlined in a Design Agreement Document.

STEP THREE
Planning

In moving forward, your Designer will guide you through the important details and decisions of your project. We will develop detailed floor plans, elevations, and a 3D rendering of your space. Next, your Designer will help you make your selections and finalize your project’s design. We will schedule a trade walk thru at your home to help ensure that everyone working on your project understands the scope and timeline. Once all the selections and design details have been finalized, we will determine a firm investment number and prepare your Building Agreement. We will also give you access to your online interactive resource, BuilderTrend.

STEP FOUR
Construction

After we receive your signed Building Agreement, all products will be ordered and your job schedule will be created. We will schedule a Pre-Construction walk thru meeting to discuss the details and expectations with you prior of the start of your project with your Project Manager. A weekly meeting will be conducted to ask for any feedback, discuss the progress of the job schedule, and to make sure we are meeting your expectations.

STEP FIVE
Completion

As your project is wrapping up, we will schedule a Substantial Completion Meeting where we will create a completion list noting any outstanding items. We will complete these items as soon as possible so you can enjoy your new space! Once you’ve had time to settle in, we would love to come back and have professional pictures taken of your newly remodeled space. We will contact you to see if there are any warranty issues that may need our attention during your 18-month warranty period.

Remodel or Move? A 2026 Guide for Oakland County Homeowners
Remodel or Move? A 2026 Guide for Oakland County Homeowners
Post Date: August 19, 2026

You like your neighborhood, but your home no longer fits the way you live. That can leave you wondering whether it is better to remodel or move.

The kitchen feels crowded. Storage is limited. You need another bedroom, a private office, or a first-floor primary suite. Your family may be growing, an older parent may need a more accessible place to live, or you may be thinking about how the house will function as you age.

Homeowners throughout Oakland County, Macomb County, and the Grosse Pointe communities are weighing the decision to remodel or move in 2026. Mortgage rates remain a factor, desirable homes can be difficult to find, and moving involves costs that extend beyond the purchase price.

For many homeowners, remodeling offers a way to create the space they need without leaving a location, property, or community they already value.

Should You Remodel or Move?

Remodeling is often the better choice when you like your location, have equity in your home, and can correct the property’s biggest limitations through a renovation or addition.

Moving may make more sense when the location no longer works, the property cannot support the changes you need, or you want a completely different type of home.

The decision should account for more than the estimated renovation cost or the listing price of another property. You also need to compare mortgage payments, selling expenses, closing costs, property taxes, renovation needs, and how long you expect to remain in the home.

The right choice depends on whether your current property can become the home you need.

Why More Southeast Michigan Homeowners Are Considering Remodeling

Many homeowners purchased or refinanced their homes when mortgage rates were lower. Selling may mean replacing that mortgage with a higher-rate loan, even if the next home is not substantially more expensive.

Moving also introduces several additional expenses:

Real estate commissions and selling costs
Mortgage closing costs
Inspections and appraisals
Moving services
Repairs or updates before listing
Higher property taxes or homeowners insurance
Improvements needed in the next home

The replacement property may offer more square footage but still need a kitchen renovation, bathroom updates, better storage, new flooring, or mechanical work.

Remodeling allows homeowners to preserve the parts of their current property that already work while correcting the parts that do not.

This is especially relevant in established communities such as Rochester Hills, Troy, Birmingham, Bloomfield Hills, Royal Oak, Washington Township, Shelby Township, Oakland Township, Lake Orion, and the Grosse Pointes, where homeowners may place significant value on their neighborhood, lot, school district, commute, or proximity to family.

Limited Inventory Can Make Moving More Difficult

Selling your home does not guarantee that the right replacement property will be available.

A family may need four bedrooms, a larger kitchen, a home office, a first-floor primary suite, and enough outdoor space for children or pets. Finding all of those features in the right location and price range can be difficult.

Compromise is part of buying a home. The question is whether those compromises create a meaningful improvement over the home you already own.

A different house may provide another bedroom but have a smaller yard. It may have an updated kitchen but create a longer commute. It may be in the right neighborhood but require substantial renovations after closing.

Remodeling provides more control over the outcome. Instead of searching for a property that comes close to meeting your needs, you can design your current home around the way your household lives.

Start by Identifying What Is Not Working

Do not begin by asking whether you need an addition or a larger house. Begin by identifying the problems you want to solve.

Common reasons homeowners consider remodeling include:

A kitchen that is too small or disconnected from the living area
Too few bedrooms or bathrooms
Limited pantry, closet, or mudroom storage
No dedicated office for remote work
An underused dining room or formal living room
A primary bedroom located on the second floor
Poor traffic flow between the main living spaces
Accessibility concerns
Not enough room for guests or extended family

Some of these problems can be solved within the existing footprint. Others may require additional square footage.

A design professional can evaluate the layout, structure, plumbing, mechanical systems, natural light, and available property to determine which changes are practical.

When Is Remodeling Better Than Moving?

Remodeling is usually worth serious consideration when the home’s problems can be corrected and the location remains a good fit.

You Want to Stay in Your Community

Location is the one part of a home that cannot be remodeled.

You may value your school district, commute, property, nearby family, or access to local amenities. You may also have a larger lot, mature landscaping, water access, or an established relationship with your neighbors.

These qualities can be difficult to recreate somewhere else.

Oakland County, Macomb County, and the Grosse Pointes also contain homes built across many architectural styles and periods. Older colonials, ranches, lake homes, Tudors, mid-century properties, and homes built during the 1980s and 1990s each present different renovation opportunities.

Our guide to what makes Oakland County homes unique to remodel explains how architectural style, construction methods, lot conditions, and previous renovations can influence a project. Many of those considerations also apply to homes throughout Macomb County and the Grosse Pointe communities.

Your Home Has a Workable Structure

A house does not always need more square footage. Sometimes it needs a better layout.

Separate kitchens, narrow openings, underused dining rooms, and disconnected living areas can make a home feel smaller than it is.

Removing or repositioning walls may improve traffic flow and create a stronger connection between the kitchen, dining area, and family room. Reallocating existing space may also create a pantry, mudroom, laundry room, office, or larger primary bathroom.

A kitchen renovation can solve several problems at once by improving storage, lighting, seating, and circulation. Homeowners considering a kitchen project can review our guide to kitchen features homeowners wish they had included and explore our kitchen remodeling services.

You Have Built Equity in the Property

Long-term homeowners may have substantial equity available in their homes.

That equity may create financing options for a renovation without requiring the property to be sold. Depending on the homeowner’s financial position, those options could include savings, a home equity loan, or a home equity line of credit.

Every financing option has different rates, repayment terms, fees, and risks. Discuss those choices with a qualified lender or financial professional.

The project should also be evaluated against the home’s current value, surrounding market, renovation scope, and the number of years you expect to remain there.

Our article about remodeling costs and what homeowners should plan to invest explains the factors that influence Project Investment, including structural changes, material selections, design complexity, and existing conditions.

You Plan to Stay for Several Years

A major remodel makes more sense when your household expects to use and enjoy the finished space for several years.

The return is not limited to future resale value. It also includes better storage, improved traffic flow, greater comfort, fewer daily frustrations, and a home that supports your routines.

A larger kitchen may create room for family gatherings. A first-floor suite may allow someone to remain in the home longer. A private office may improve the workday. A functional mudroom may make daily arrivals and departures easier.

These benefits have real value, even when they cannot be measured through resale figures alone.

When Is Moving Better Than Remodeling?

Renovation cannot solve every problem.

Moving may be the better decision when your concerns are tied to the location, property, or overall type of home rather than the interior layout.

The Location No Longer Fits Your Life

A remodel cannot shorten a difficult commute, change the school district, move the home closer to family, or create a larger property.

Your priorities may also have changed. You may want to live in a more walkable community, move closer to downtown, find more acreage, or reduce exterior maintenance.

When the location itself is the problem, investing heavily in the house may only delay an eventual move.

The Property Cannot Support the Renovation

Municipal requirements can limit what may be built.

Setbacks, lot coverage, building height, drainage requirements, septic systems, utility locations, homeowner association rules, and historic district guidelines can all affect a home addition.

These requirements vary between municipalities in Oakland County, Macomb County, and the Grosse Pointes.

The existing structure may also limit certain plans. Building upward could require substantial reinforcement. Expanding outward may eliminate too much yard space. Moving plumbing or mechanical systems may use a large portion of the available Project Investment.

These conditions do not always rule out renovation, but they should be identified early.

You Want a Completely Different Type of Home

Sometimes the desired change is too large for a practical renovation.

A growing family may want significantly more land and square footage. Empty nesters may prefer a smaller ranch or condominium. A homeowner may want a waterfront property, a different school district, or a lower-maintenance lifestyle.

Remodeling works best when the current house and property provide a strong foundation for the next stage of your life.

“Remodeling is not always the right answer. Moving is not always the easier answer. The best choice depends on whether your existing property can become the home you need.”
Can a Home Addition Be Better Than Moving?

A home addition can create a middle ground between accepting an inadequate floor plan and purchasing another property.

Common additions include:

Expanded kitchens and gathering areas
First-floor primary suites
Family rooms
Home offices
Mudrooms
Additional bedrooms and bathrooms
In-law suites
Second-story expansions
Space for multigenerational living

A family in Rochester Hills may need a larger kitchen and mudroom. Homeowners in Washington Township may want a first-floor primary suite. A Grosse Pointe family may want to expand an older home while preserving its architectural character.

A well-designed addition should look and function like part of the original house. Rooflines, exterior materials, windows, interior transitions, mechanical systems, and room proportions all need to work together.

The existing floor plan should also be reconsidered. Adding square footage without correcting the original layout can leave homeowners with a larger house that still does not function well.

Learn more about five ways to add space without moving, review our guide to planning a home addition in Michigan, or explore Renovation By Design’s home addition services.

Can You Remodel for Aging in Place?

Remodeling can make it possible to remain in a familiar home safely and comfortably as you age.

A house that works today may become difficult to navigate later. Stairs, narrow doorways, slippery bathroom floors, poor lighting, and a second-floor primary bedroom can become significant obstacles.

Aging-in-place improvements may include:

A first-floor primary suite
A main-floor laundry room
Wider doorways
More accessible storage
Better lighting
Safer flooring transitions
Lever-style door hardware
A curbless or low-threshold shower
Wall reinforcement for future grab bars

These features do not need to make a home feel institutional. They can be incorporated into a functional and attractive design.

Our guide to accessible and aging-in-place bathroom design covers layout, safety, mobility, and long-term use. You can also explore our bathroom remodeling services.

Planning these changes before they become urgent gives homeowners more control over the result and reduces the need for rushed decisions later.

What About a Whole-Home Remodel?

A whole-home remodel may be appropriate when several parts of the house no longer work together.

The kitchen may be closed off. Storage may be limited. Flooring may change from room to room. The primary bathroom may need to be redesigned. Lighting may be poor, and the main living areas may lack a consistent appearance.

Completing each project separately over many years can create duplicated work, inconsistent materials, and repeated disruption.

A whole-home plan allows the design team to consider how the entire property functions. Flooring, cabinetry, lighting, trim, structural changes, mechanical systems, and room layouts can be coordinated from the beginning.

The work may still be completed in phases, but each phase supports one long-term vision.

How Do You Compare the Cost of Remodeling and Moving?

Compare both options using a complete financial picture.

For moving, include:

The purchase price of the next home
The interest rate and estimated mortgage payment
Property taxes and homeowners insurance
Real estate commissions and selling expenses
Closing costs
Inspections and appraisals
Moving expenses
Repairs needed before listing
Improvements required after purchasing the next home

For remodeling, include:

Design and planning
Engineering
Permits
Materials
Construction labor
Structural work
Temporary living arrangements, if needed
An appropriate contingency for concealed conditions

Older homes may contain aging plumbing, outdated electrical systems, previous structural changes, water damage, or work that does not meet current building standards. Some conditions may not be visible until walls, floors, or ceilings are opened.

A coordinated design+build process helps identify likely challenges and align the design with the intended Project Investment before construction begins.

Our guide to the design+build process for Southeast Michigan homeowners explains how Renovation By Design takes a project from the initial consultation through design, planning, construction, and the final walkthrough.

Remodel or Move Checklist

Ask these questions before making your decision:

Do we want to remain in this community for at least five more years?
Are our concerns primarily about the house or the location?
Can the existing floor plan be reorganized?
Can the lot and structure support an addition?
What would our mortgage payment be if we moved?
What selling, closing, and moving expenses would we incur?
Would another home still require renovations?
How much equity do we have in the current property?
Are we planning for children, aging parents, remote work, or retirement?
Which option provides the best daily life and long-term flexibility?

You do not need to know exactly what the finished renovation should look like before speaking with a design+build company.

You need to know what is not working, what your priorities are, and how long you expect to remain in the home.

What Are Local Homeowners Choosing in 2026?

Many homeowners throughout Oakland County, Macomb County, and the Grosse Pointe communities are choosing to explore remodeling before putting their homes on the market.

They may not want to give up a favorable mortgage, established neighborhood, larger lot, or strong community connection. They also recognize that purchasing another property may introduce a different set of compromises and renovation needs.

Remodeling is not always the right answer. Moving is not always the easier answer.

The best choice depends on whether your existing property can become the home you need.

About Us

Hello there! We’re the proud owners of SH Renovations, a veteran-owned business that’s been serving the Norman and The Greater Oklahoma City area since 2018. We specialize in all types of remodeling projects, from transforming kitchens and bathrooms to creating more living space where you’d least expect it.

Our journey started out of a passion for helping people turn their houses into homes. We’ve faced challenges along the way, but the smiles on our clients’ faces when they see their dreams turned into reality makes it all worth it.

We’re not just a business, we’re a family. Our team is a group of dedicated professionals who are passionate about delivering high-quality results that exceed expectations. Each member brings a unique skill set to our projects, and we couldn’t be prouder of the work we do together.

But don’t just take our word for it, hear what our clients have to say:

Great experience with Hunter! Easy to use online portal helped us to track costs and all parts of the process were really transparent. All the crews were professional and especially patient with our yappy dogs. Kitchen reno looks fab! Highly recommend SH Renovations!

Kim P.

Hunter and his team are some of the best in Norman! Professional from start to finish and they took the time to make sure every detail was to our liking. I couldn't be happier with how our projects turned out. Our business exclusively uses SH and we definitely would recommend! Thanks again!

Aaliyah H.

Hunter and has his team were amazing to work with! They were very professional. They took extra precautions to protect our home while they worked in it. Hunter walked us through the entire process and made sure to get our input on every detail, including the little things that we didn’t think of. We love our outdoor space and master bathroom remodel! It is scary and hard to find a new contractor but we are very happy we chose SH Renovations!

Dennis G.

We’re not here to just do a job – we’re here to bring your vision to life. We listen, understand your preferences, and use our knowledge to deliver a result that we’re sure you’ll love.

Rest assured, we’re fully licensed and insured, and we stand behind our work with a satisfaction guarantee. We’re passionate about what we do and dedicated to providing exceptional service.

So why not join our family of satisfied clients? Contact us today to schedule a consultation and let’s transform your space together.

Hunter Thompson - Founder and Owner of SH Renovations

Hunter Thompson, the heart and soul behind SH Renovations, brings more than just expertise to his work. He brings a deep-rooted passion for transforming spaces and lives. His journey began in Jacksonville, NC, in the aftermath of Hurricane Florence. Disturbed by the unprofessional behavior and fraud he observed in the industry, Hunter was inspired to restore respect and professionalism, and thus SH Renovations was born.

Before diving into the world of home renovations, Hunter served as a machine gunner in the infantry of the U.S. Marine Corps for four years, right out of high school. This experience instilled in him a strong sense of discipline and a relentless drive to succeed, qualities that have become fundamental to SH Renovations’ success. Hunter’s commitment to excellent service and his passion for transforming outdated spaces into beautiful, functional homes have made SH Renovations a trusted name in the industry.

One of Hunter’s most memorable projects was a full kitchen, bathroom, and addition for a family whose son, a wounded army veteran, is bedridden. The project not only transformed the home but also brought joy and comfort to a deserving family. It’s these moments that make the work truly fulfilling for Hunter.

When he’s not transforming homes, Hunter can be found enjoying family time with his wife and three children or fishing on the local Norman Lake Thunderbird. He’s also an avid cook and enjoys smoking meat for OU football gatherings.

Hunter’s personal philosophy is that “Failing to prepare is preparing to fail.” This mantra guides his approach to his work and is reflected in the meticulous planning and execution of each project at SH Renovations.

Looking to the future, Hunter aspires to expand SH Renovations into custom home building and larger projects, further extending the company’s reach into the community. His vision is not just to grow the business, but also to increase community involvement and make a positive impact on more lives.

Who is Chapter Renovation?
Founding vision

Chapter Renovation emerged from the shared vision of its founders, who both hail from extensive backgrounds in real estate development and construction. Through their firsthand experiences with the renovation process across various locations, they encountered the common pain points faced by clients. Recognizing the inefficiencies and communication breakdowns, they envisioned a more streamlined and client-centric approach.

The creation of Chapter Renovation

Our vision led to the creation of Chapter Renovation, a design-build company that revolutionizes the way renovations are conducted. By consolidating all stakeholders into a single entity, Chapter Renovation seamlessly manages the renovation journey from conception to execution. This integrated model eliminates miscommunication and enhances efficiency.

Our story began in NYC

Our roots are in one of the hardest-to-renovate-in cities in the nation. A place where pre-construction planning is king, and you’re only destined for success when you know the barriers you’re planning to avoid. After establishing ourselves as a leading renovation company in NYC, we are now expanding our proven renovation approach to other cities across the nation.

Innovation and transparency

Our curated, innovative technology solutions—designed with the client in mind—mark a significant leap forward in making the renovation process as smooth and stress-free as possible. With a customized client portal updating all essential project information, this technology ensures transparency throughout the entire renovation process.

OUR PROCESS
Consultation

This informational gathering meeting is the foundation for the estimating and design phases to follow. The main goal is to learn everything possible about our client’s personalities, lifestyles, and needs. We also determine how much space you need now and are likely to need in the future, and how that space should be used, organized, and arranged. 

Present Estimate and Predesign

With your estimate, we present ideas using images from other projects and hand sketches to help visualize the size, shape, and relationship of spaces to each other.

Timing: 2 weeks

Estimate Approval

Upon estimate approval, we will refine the predesign according to clients’ feedback until we reach an agreed-upon design direction to develop further. 

Timing: 1-2 weeks

Design Development 

During Design Development we talk more specifically about materials and finishes. This phase is usually when our clients feel the project coming to life and it becomes possible to see themselves in the new space. By the end of the Design Development phase, the interior layout will be completed, the dimensions of all spaces finalized, and materials selected. 

Timing: 1-2 weeks

Materials Procurement 

ICDC will order all materials and set a start date based on ETA’s and our current workload. 

Construction Documents

In this phase, we develop the Design Drawings into a thorough set of documents. These drawings and specifications have all of the details, dimensions, and notes necessary to communicate the entire design intent to our build team. 

Timing: 1-2 weeks

Permitting

If permitting is necessary, we add to the construction documents any additional information required to get a building permit. We submit these drawings along with the various forms required for the permit application to the local plans reviewer, monitor the progress during the review period, and give additional information or clarifications as requested. 

Timing: could be 8-12 weeks

Pre-Build Meeting

A planning session with the project manager, contractors, designer, and clients will occur prior to construction beginning to answer questions and proactively address potential issues. At this time, clients will be given access to our construction management platform, used to connect our team, clients and subs so everyone can stay updated throughout the project. 

The Build

Based on project timelines will vary greatly. Throughout the process, your Project Manager will be your main point of contact for any scheduling and questions regarding the build process. The designer will make regular visits to the project ensuring the finished project meets all expectations. Inevitably, some decisions must be made or modified in the field, being a team allows us to work quickly to solve problems, which is essential for helping you avoid costly delays and change orders.  At the end of the project, we help you develop your final punch list to ensure all work is completed to your satisfaction. 

In-depth meetings and collaborations with our clients help us account for their needs and tastes, our design team provides comprehensive interior design services from spatial planning and fixture selection.

IC Design Co manages all aspects of construction, including quality, schedule, and budget. We solve the problems that arise during construction and effectively communicate with all parties throughout the process. Our expertise and experience allow us to excel in environments that are multi-phased or require a high level of planning.

As your construction partner, ICDC coordinates the endless details required by construction projects of any size. We collaborate with design professionals, consultants, and subcontractors to maximize our ability to provide accurate estimating, knowledgeable scheduling, efficient permitting, cost-effective material purchasing, and creative value engineering.

Meet Our Team
Founder of Rosewood Remodeling Company LLC
Kevin Remson

 

Kevin Remson is the innovative driving force behind Rosewood Remodeling. His career journey is a testament to his dedication and passion for beauty, style, and functionality. Kevin’s career began humbly, with early work experiences ranging from being a cashier to delivering pizzas, laying the foundation for his robust work ethic and unwavering commitment to customer service.

Kevin’s carpentry career took off in 1986, marking the beginning of a lifelong passion for creating exceptional living spaces. Over the years, he has founded, purchased, and rebranded various carpentry companies, including Heritage Carpentry and Homecare Remodeling Company LLC. With over thirty years of experience leading diverse creative teams in carpentry, Kevin’s expertise and leadership skills are unparalleled. He has consistently worked to design and shape homes that reflect their owners’ personalities, styles, and tastes.

In February 2014, Kevin founded Rosewood Remodeling Company LLC, where he leverages his extensive knowledge and skills as a Project Manager to deliver top-notch remodeling services. His vision for Rosewood Remodeling goes beyond mere construction; he sees houses as living storybooks, each with its own unique narrative and history.

Kevin is particularly fascinated by what homes can tell about the families that have lived in them—whether it’s family holidays, celebrations, or other significant events. This deep appreciation for a home’s story drives his commitment to preserving and enhancing these spaces rather than tearing them down.

At Rosewood Remodeling, our goal is to be the savior of these houses, creating new pages for their stories to continue with families who will love and care for them for generations to come. We believe in the power of thoughtful remodeling to transform homes into places where new memories are made. We are dedicated to maintaining the integrity and character of every project we undertake, ensuring that each home we touch continues to be a cherished part of its community for many years to come.

About Clar Construction

Since 2004, Clar Construction has established itself as a leader in crafting bespoke living spaces. We have expertly remodeled homes, crafted custom additions, decks, cabinetry, and built-ins, ensuring every detail reflects our commitment to excellence. Our dedicated team, which includes skilled production staff, esteemed partners, reliable vendors, and our meticulous administrative professionals, stands ready to elevate your home to new heights.

Our approach sets us apart. We believe in transparency and meticulous planning. From the conceptualization phase, we work hand in hand with our clients, ensuring that every detail is outlined and understood. This collaborative method ensures clarity on costs and overall project expectations from the outset, guaranteeing a harmonious journey towards realizing your home’s potential.

Our Shop & Office Located Downtown Montpelier

Our headquarters is nestled within the historic National Clothespin Company building on Granite Street in Montpelier. Before we took residence, the company had processed its final 10,000 board feet of maple on machinery once used to craft the iconic spring-loaded clothespin — a hallmark Vermont invention from 1853.

In the time since the National Clothespin Company’s departure, we have been meticulously transforming this once-traditional woodworking establishment into a state-of-the-art millwork facility. We are immensely proud to carry on the tradition of crafting wood-based materials, now for our home remodeling clients, in this very space where wooden clothespins were once manufactured. The space itself is luminous, with abundant natural light, and it’s steeped in a century’s worth of industrial heritage — evident in its walls and floors.

Step 1: Get To Know Each Other

Whether our prospective clients call, email, or walk in the office, there is always a conversation where we will start to learn about each other. We find that people considering a project for their home sometimes have very distinct ideas about what they’d like to do, while others have a sense that they need something about their home to change to better satisfy their lifestyle. 

We’ll ask the questions that will allow you to share whatever your current thinking is. We’ll also likely suggest some other ideas that you may want to consider.

UNDERSTANDING OUR PROCESS

During this meeting, we will share with you the general outline of our process and determine if this Design-Build is a method you are comfortable with.

BUDGET DISCUSSION

We’ll also want to talk about the amount of money you’re considering investing in your home and how that amount relates to the price of similar projects we’ve already completed. We’ll suggest a range of costs during this initial consultation, or if the project has some complexity to it, we’ll set another meeting within a week to review what we think this price range will be.

ALIGNING OUR GOALS

If that price range is not consistent with your expectations, we’ll talk about ways to alter the scope to meet the budget goals. Or perhaps we’ll agree that we’re not a good fit for each other. That’s ok- It doesn’t always work! If we do agree that the budgeting goals are consistent with what we believe the price of the project will likely be, then we’ll ask you to enter into our Project Development Agreement.

Step 2: Project Development Agreement

The objective of the Project Development phase is to produce a project scope that meets the goals of the project.

DESIGN & PLANNING MEETINGS

Now that we’ve committed to working together within a target budget, we begin a series of meetings in which we will identify the scope of the project. Certain types of projects will engage one of the designers or architects we work with, while other types of projects will be designed with our in house staff.

It is through a series of meetings that we collaboratively establish exactly what it is that will be built for you– from the floor plan right down to the grout color and towel bars.

This is the way we know to make sure that everything will be accounted for both from the perspective of the user (there needs to be a place to hang the towel!) but equally important is that it is only when we identify all of these details that we can confidently provide the fixed price model that we work within.

During this process, we engage our trade partners and vendors to provide their expertise as we work to establish the scope and product selections. We’ll also talk about specific needs that may be uniquely important to your family and you – things like dust control, snow clearing, and accommodations that may need to be made for children or pets. You, of course, can decide to alter the goals of the project along the way – we’ll be clear to discuss the financial implications.

When we reach the end of the Project Development phase and see that everyone’s goals are in alignment, the next step is to commit to the construction agreement.

Step 3: The Construction Phase

CONSTRUCTION BEGINS

This is the step we have been working toward since the start of the project planning! One of our lead carpenters (who you will have already met) will be assigned to your project, and he or she will be your point person during construction. 

Our in house team of carpentry staff works in conjunction with a team of subcontractors that fulfill the specialty/licensed trades (electrical, plumbing, roofing, etc.).

COORDINATING OUR SCHEDULES

Everyone who is part of your project will be properly insured. We will progress through the various stages of your project with the lead carpenter orchestrating the schedule. You will receive periodic updates on what to expect for progress over the upcoming weeks and which trades will be working on your home.

All of the planning that we collaborated on pays off during the construction phase, minimizing questions (though there will still be some!) and supporting smooth progress and quality craftsmanship during the project.

Step 4: Project Completion & Warranty

FINALIZING YOUR PROJECT

Our clients are typically pretty excited to see us arrive at their home to start building their project. And we know that they’re similarly excited to see us go so they can begin enjoying their newly remodeled home. We’ll do everything we can to be as efficient with our scheduling as possible so you can start living in your space again without us as your daily guest! 

After all, this is the reason we’ve previously spent so much time regarding the upfront planning of the project during the PDA phase — it allows us to return your home to you in its new condition as quickly as possible.

We have the end of your project in our view from the day we begin it. As we approach the end of your project, we will schedule a time to meet with you to discuss any outstanding items that need to be completed to ensure that everyone experiences the project as a success. 

We’ll have our list of things to do, and you’ll have the opportunity to bring ideas to our attention that might be on your list. This way, we can address these items, while all of our resources are still at your home.

Celebrating 20 Years of Remodeling

Share this article:

Facebook
 
Pinterest
 
Twitter
 
Email
This year marks a significant milestone for Clar Construction as we celebrate two decades of dedication and craftsmanship in the Montpelier community.

Since our founding in 2004, we’ve had the privilege of transforming countless homes, enhancing both their functionality and beauty. As we reflect on these years, we are overwhelmed with gratitude towards you—our valued clients, vendors, and subcontractors—for your unwavering support and partnership.

Two Decades of Growth & Success

It’s been an incredible journey from our early days to now. Our portfolio has grown to include everything from cozy kitchen remodels to expansive home additions.

Renovation to our headquarters at the historic Clothingspin Factory building has begun!  This year is particularly momentous as we’ve purchased and begun the renovation of the historic Clothespin Factory building, which many of you know as our long-term home. We’re not only renovating our workspace but also revitalizing the structure to host and house: 

Art studios
A movement center
Professional offices

With the hopes of breathing new life into this beloved Montpelier landmark.

The historic Clothingspin Factory located Downtown Montpelier. Headquarters for Clar Construction.

A Commitment to Our Community

Our connection to Montpelier is deeper than just business. It’s about building a stronger community together. This year, as part of our 20th-anniversary celebration, we were excited to host to a special picnic at Hubbard Park for our team and our partners. This event was a chance to relax, reflect, and rejoice in our shared achievements. Additionally, we remain committed to giving back to the community that has supported us, continuing our tradition of volunteer labor to local causes.

Looking Forward

As we look to the future, Clar Construction is as dedicated as ever to enhancing our craftsmanship and serving our community. We are investing in the next generation of skilled carpenters and maintaining a workplace that supports professional growth and personal well-being.

Thank You! Here's to Another 20 Years!

Thank you for being an integral part of our journey. Without your collaboration, trust, and shared vision, these 20 years of success would not have been possible. We look forward to many more years of partnership and success.

Sincerely, 

Dan Clar
Owner
Clar Construction
